blocking_methods.label: tollFree
blocking_methods.instructions: Call 1800-258-8181 and follow the IVR to hotlist the card.

SMS Call our customer care at 18002588181 (toll free) from your registered mobile number and follow the steps/instructions by the Interactive Voice Response (IVR); SMS: "Send this SMS to 9920311246 from your mobile number registered with the Bank."
Email customercare@bandhanbank.com from your registered email to request card blocking.
Log in to internet banking at https://bandhan.bank.in/internet-banking-login and use the card block/hotlist option.
Block via the bank's mobile app (Cards > Block/Hotlist). Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.bandhan.mBandhanN | iOS: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/mbandhan-2-0/id6758432075

SMS Permanent block: type BLOCKDC <space> <Last 4 digits of your Bandhan Bank Debit Card number> and send to 9920311246 (example: BLOCKDC 1234). Temporary block: type TBLCKDC <space> <Last 4 digits> and send to 9920311246 (example: TBLCKDC 1234). from your registered mobile number.

IVR self-service on the toll-free line from your registered mobile: press 2 for temporary block (OTP required) or 1 for permanent block, select the card from the prompted list; a confirmation SMS follows. SMS banking to 9920311246: BLOCKDC (permanent) or TBLCKDC (temporary) plus last 4 digits. Internet Banking or mBandhan 2.0 app path: Discover Product > Debit Card > Manage Card > Block/Unblock Card > Temporary or Permanent Block (Hotlist) > Submit; email customercare@bandhanbank.com for a permanent block; branch permanent block needs a written consent application (Customer ID, Account Number, Card Number last four digits). Alternate customer-care lines: 033-6633-3333 (the bank's fraud-awareness page says it can be used from India and abroad) and 033-4409-9090 (listed with 18002588181 / 03366333333 / 03340903333 as customer-care numbers in the bank's FAQ, and shown as 'Customer care no.' in the credit-card microsite footer). No explicit hotline service hours are stated on the bank's live contact, grievance or FAQ pages (checked 2026-10-27); the credit-card microsite's fraud-safety article states 'Bandhan Bank has 24/7 customer support'. The bank's fraud-awareness page directs fraud victims to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in.

blocking_methods.label: tollFree
blocking_methods.instructions: Call 1800-258-8181 and follow the IVR to hotlist the card.
Email creditcard.customercare@bandhanbank.com from your registered email to request card blocking.
Log in to internet banking at https://bandhan.bank.in/internet-banking-login and use the card block/hotlist option.
SMS SMS BLOCKCC followed by last 4 digits of your card to 9920311246 (official example: BLOCKCC1234 to 9920311246). from your registered mobile number.

Block via Internet Banking, mBandhan 2.0 app, or Customer Service on 1800-258-8181; SMS option BLOCKCC + last 4 digits to 9920311246 (bank's credit-card FAQ). App/netbanking menu path (bank's main-site FAQ): hamburger menu > Discover Products > Credit Cards > block/unblock card page > select card > 'Temporary Block' or 'Permanent Block' from the dropdown > Submit > Confirm, with 6-digit OTP (Internet Banking) or 6-digit mPIN (mBandhan 2.0 app); the FAQ states a permanent credit-card block cannot be unblocked. Lost/stolen: report immediately to Customer Service at 1800-258-8181; the card can also be blocked and replaced from the mBandhan 2.0 app or Internet Banking. For suspicious/fraudulent transactions the bank publishes email creditcard.customercare@bandhanbank.com alongside the 1800-258-8181 line. Alternate customer-care lines: 033-6633-3333 (usable 'India and abroad' per the bank's fraud-awareness page) and 033-4409-9090 (listed with 18002588181 / 03366333333 / 03340903333 in the bank's FAQ and shown as 'Customer care no.' in the credit-card microsite footer). No explicit hotline service hours are stated on the bank's live pages (checked 2026-10-27); the microsite's fraud-safety article states 'Bandhan Bank has 24/7 customer support'. The bank's fraud-awareness page directs fraud victims to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in.
